citation_details.title: Affordance-based design evaluation: Bridging architectural intention and adaptive user behavior
citation_details.author: Mohsen Mohammadi, Alexander Koutamanis
citation_details.abstract: Affordances—the action possibilities provided by the environment—are a central notion in ecological psychology, offering valuable insights into dynamic user-environment interactions. In recent years, affordance theory has gained traction in architecture and design for its potential to illuminate how users perceive and engage with built environments, informing both design thinking and performance evaluation. Despite this growing interest, its application within architectural design research remains limited. This article introduces an affordance-based evaluation framework developed to analyze how built environments enable or constrain adaptive user behaviors. Grounded in ecological psychology and architectural theory, the framework provides a structured approach for assessing usability, anticipating behavioral variability, and aligning design outcomes with diverse user needs. citation_details.title: From Vernacular Materials To Industrial Metal Housing: Changes In Architectural Affordances and Dwelling Experiences
citation_details.author: - Aulia Khairunnisa Nada, Diah Cahyani Permana Sari, Kunthi Herma Dwidayati
citation_details.venue: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)
citation_details.abstract: The transition of housing materials from local vernacular houses to metal industrial houses in the Rumah Reflektif Surya Indonesia (RAFLESIA) offers construction efficiency but has the potential to fundamentally alter the residents dwelling experience. This study aims to identify the changes in architectural affordance (opportunities for action) experienced by residents during this transition. The study employs an exploratory qualitative case study involving two permanent residents of the RAFLESIA house in Padalarang, West Bandung Regency. Data were analyzed through affordance categorization based on the perception-function framework and the effect purpose framework. The findings confirm that affordance in the RAFLESIA house is dynamic, not fixed, and strongly influenced by material characteristics, socio-cultural background, and residents dwelling experience. citation_details.title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
citation_details.author: Junyu Pan, Ruicheng Yin, Bao‐Liang Lu, Dongsheng Li, Wei-Long Zheng, Yansen Wang
citation_details.abstract: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. Building on this foundation, we expand pretraining data and model capacity while retaining its core encoder and objective. We train ten encoders with 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections spanning 25,067 to 79,910 hours, adapting signal preparation and training to heterogeneous recordings. Across 23 tasks, Atom-L* reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy at its best evaluated full fine-tuning (Full-FT) checkpoint, 3.61 percentage points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model. Quark-G leads linear probing (LP) at 54.33%, a 1.24-point margin. Both also lead average task rank. At the last evaluated checkpoints, larger encoders improve Full-FT more consistently than LP, and stronger LP does not guarantee stronger Full-FT.
